evidence: Figure 2.2 caption, book page 32 (PDF p.56): "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — both plotted intensities are computed from the stated inputs, not measured"
issue: Provenance label mismatch. The Preface (p.14) defines [ILLUSTRATIVE] as "a non-canonical worked example or scenario input chosen to make a calculation concrete" and [canonical scenario] as "the book's own internally defined workload and model (Ch. 4, Table 4-2)." Both plotted intensities — prefill ~9,200 FLOP/byte (= 1.29 PFLOP / 140 GB) and decode ~1 FLOP/byte (= 140 GFLOP / 140 GB) — are computed from the canonical scenario's own inputs (Table 4-2: 70B model, 9,200 tokens, FP16, H100 specs). The caption itself says they are "computed from the stated inputs." Per the Preface's rule (p.16: "a value arithmetically derived from those assumed inputs ... is [canonical scenario][DERIVED]"), the correct provenance should be [canonical scenario][DERIVED], not [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]. The same pattern recurs on Figure 1.1 (PDF p.56, "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch. 4, Table 4-2)") and Figure 2.1 (PDF p.44, "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT], Ch 4)") — all three label canonical-scenario-derived content with the non-canonical provenance tag.
fix_instruction: Change [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] to [canonical scenario][DERIVED] on Figure 2.2's caption where the label specifically attributes to "both plotted intensities." For Figures 1.1 and 2.1, where [ILLUSTRATIVE] may describe the schematic artifact (a simplified drawing) rather than the data, either add a clarifying note that [ILLUSTRATIVE] refers to the drawing's simplification (not the data provenance) or restructure the label to separate figure-artifact provenance from data provenance. Recurrence sweep: check all figure captions that carry [ILLUSTRATIVE] but whose plotted/drawn values derive from Table 4-2.

page: PDF p. 38 (printed 14) and PDF p. 60 (printed 36); convention stated at PDF p. 20 (printed xvi)
evidence: PDF p. 38 (Ch. 1, §1.5, Common Mistakes): "code, numerics, and non-Latin scripts can run 2–5× the naive word-count estimate (rule of thumb; the multiplier is tokenizer- and language-specific) [ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark][HYPOTHESIS]". The Preface's label rules (PDF p. 20) state: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the two tags are set with no space between them and never break across a line", and the Axis-1 vocabulary is the closed set "[1P] / [canonical scenario] / [ILLUSTRATIVE] / [2°] / [LAB]".
issue: Two occurrences embed free prose inside the provenance tag ("[ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark]"), which is not a member of the book's own closed Axis-1 vocabulary and breaks the mandatory one-tag-per-axis, no-space, no-inline-text pair format. The qualifier belongs in the surrounding prose, not inside the brackets. The defect is not cosmetic for this book: the Preface's whole verification scheme depends on labels being machine-parseable tokens, and the second occurrence also stacks a third bracket ([UNMEASURED]) onto a pair, which the Preface permits only as a third axis 'riding along' rather than appended as free text.
fix_instruction: Replace both with the bare tag pair and move the qualifier into the prose immediately before it — e.g. "an industry rule of thumb, with no named survey or benchmark [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]" — and re-check the whole document for any other occurrence of a bracketed tag containing a colon or free text (search for "[ILLUSTRATIVE:" and "[1P:").

page: PDF p. 41 (printed 17) vs PDF p. 32 (printed 8); convention noted at PDF p. 22 (printed xviii)
evidence: PDF p. 41 (Ch. 2, §2.1): "The full prefill also has a substantial linear-in-L component — the weight-matmul FLOPs, 2NL (where N = model parameters and L = tokens processed)" — and the same chapter uses L for sequence length again on PDF p. 41: "the attention work grows with the square of the context length" and PDF p. 32 (Ch. 1): "4·n_layers·L·d FLOPs ... 4·n_layers·L·d bytes". Against this, PDF p. 32 (Ch. 1, KV cache section) states: "(The symbol is Mweights, not W: throughout the book W is reserved for mean time in system in Little's law, L = λW, Ch 4.)" — i.e. L is also the Little's-law population of requests in system, as it is in Ch. 2's own use of "L = λW" and in Ch. 4's "Lexec = λ × Wexec".
issue: L carries two unrelated meanings across the same chapters: sequence length (tokens processed) in the FLOP/byte formulas — 2NL, 4·n_layers·L·d, 4·n_layers·L²·d — and the number of requests resident in the system in Little's law (L = λW). The book anticipated one half of this collision (it reserves W against Mweights) but left L doubly bound, and the collision lands inside one chapter: a reader following Ch. 2's "2NL" and then the same chapter's "L = λW" has to re-derive which L applies. Ch. 4 already avoids it by renaming the population L_exec, so the fix is available in the book's own vocabulary.
fix_instruction: Adopt the Ch. 4 convention book-wide: use L_exec (or N_in_system) for the Little's-law population in every occurrence — the Ch. 2 note on PDF p. 32 and the causal-chain/Little's-law passages in Ch. 2 and Ch. 4 — and state both bindings in the Preface's reading conventions next to the existing "Mweights, not W" note, so that 2NL and L = λW can never be confused.

evidence: Figure 3.4 caption states: "Resident weight... is ~94 GB... the always-on attention/shared block of ~1.4B ≈ 2.8 GB (1.4B × 2 bytes; the figure rounds that block to 3 GB)." and "the ~23 GB and the 25.6 GB are not competing [values]... Per-token read traffic... is 12.8B × 2 bytes = 25.6 GB". Table 3-2 row "FP16 active weight-read per token (batch-1 decode)" lists "~25.6 GB". Table 3-3 row "FP16 weight-read per token (batch-1 decode)" lists "~25.6 GB".
issue: Cross-chapter inconsistency in arithmetic basis for MoE active weight read traffic. Ch. 3 consistently calculates the active weight read (~25.6 GB) using a 'component-derived' total of ~47B (implying ~1.4B always-on + ~45.6B experts), whereas the vendor-published Mixtral 8x7B configuration used for the KV cache calculation in the same chapter (32 layers, hidden 4096) implies a much smaller always-on block (~0.7B). If the vendor-spec geometry were applied to the weight read, the active traffic would be ~24.2 GB, not 25.6 GB. Ch. 3 mixes a '47B total' (which requires a larger embedding/projection layer than the 4096-hidden config supports) with a '4096-hidden' attention geometry, creating a phantom discrepancy in the active weight read baseline. The 'canonical' dense 70B uses a constructed geometry (8192 hidden) that is explicitly labeled as teaching, but the MoE example conflates the published 46.7B/12.9B totals with the published 4096-hidden config without reconciling the implied always-on size.
fix_instruction: Explicitly state in the caption or Table 3-2 derivation that the ~25.6 GB active weight read is derived from the component-split (~1.4B always-on) required to reach the ~47B total, and note that this ~1.4B assumption is inconsistent with the published 4096-hidden architecture (which would imply ~0.7B always-on and ~24.2 GB active read). Flag this as a known modeling simplification in the 'Worked example, not reference' header.
